<reason>A builds the stronger decision rule: proceed despite objections only where restoration is worthwhile, implementation is feasible, and livelihoods are protected. It answers enforcement and cancellation pressure directly. B raises substantial trust and poaching risks, but repeatedly assumes community opposition necessarily prevents cooperation. Its closing equation of cooperation with consent sidesteps A’s central distinction. B also continues calling consultation predetermined despite A’s explicit cancellation conditions. A therefore better justifies why objections deserve accommodation without becoming decisive authority over shared ecological benefits.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s closing distinguishes community approval from sufficient cooperation: residents can oppose predators while participating in workable management. This directly undermines B’s claim that every viable project already satisfies its consent rule. B’s “consent wearing a frown” response relabels that scenario rather than disproving it.</best_rebuttal>
